recommendations.title: Discretionary spend is ~33% above the UK average for couples
recommendations.rationale: You're spending around £720/month on recreation, dining, and entertainment vs a UK couple average of £540. London skews this benchmark, but it's still worth knowing where the gap is. If even £100/month of this is reflexive rather than deliberate, redirecting it could matter.
recommendations.expectedImpact: Redirecting £100/month into investments could bring your FIRE date forward by ~1 year.

recommendations.title: Your Other category looks unusually high — worth investigating
recommendations.rationale: The Other bucket came in at £275/month vs a typical £75. This often means there are subscriptions, fees, or one-offs we haven't categorised. A 30-minute audit of the last 3 months could surface where this is going.
recommendations.expectedImpact: If half of this is recoverable, that's ~£100/month back — same as recommendation 1, additive.

recommendations.title: Confirm you're capturing your full employer pension match
recommendations.rationale: Your savings rate is healthy at 29%, but the single highest-leverage move for most employees is making sure they're not leaving any employer match on the table. If your employer matches above what you currently contribute, increasing to capture it is essentially a guaranteed return.
recommendations.expectedImpact: Worth checking before any other change — could be the cheapest year of FIRE you'll ever buy.
